title: Aspect 3: Aspect in the Past Tense
titleRussian: Виды глагола 3: Виды в прошедшем времени
description: The past tense is where aspect choice matters most. Today: drilling imperfective vs perfective past with gender and number agreement.
descriptionRussian: Прошедшее время — основной контекст для выбора вида. Сегодня: формы прошедшего времени НСВ и СВ с согласованием в роде и числе.
intro: The past tense is where aspect does the most work, because both aspects live there and you have to pick one every time you open your mouth. The endings themselves are the ones you already know from the past-tense book, and they do not care which aspect you chose. The whole decision happens before the ending, in which verb of the pair you reach for.
rules: Past-tense endings are the same for both aspects: -л (masc), -ла (fem), -ло (neut), -ли (plural). Gender / number agreement is with the subject, not the object.
The imperfective past describes ongoing action, duration, process, or habit / repetition.
The perfective past describes a completed action with a result, a single completed event, or a sequence of finished events.
First-person я picks gender by speaker: male says 'Я читал,' female says 'Я читала.'
examples: Маша читала книгу всё утро. (Masha was reading the book all morning.) НСВ past, fem -ла.
Антон прочитал книгу. (Anton finished the book.) СВ past, masc -л.
Мы делали уроки два часа. (We did homework for two hours.) НСВ past, plural -ли.
Они уже сделали работу. (They already finished the work.) СВ past, plural -ли.
Я писала письмо. (I (fem speaker) was writing a letter.) НСВ past, fem -ла.
Маша и Антон пришли вовремя. (Masha and Anton arrived on time.) СВ past, plural -ли.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 2: a single utterance is one completed event. Suppletive pair.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 2: говорить / сказать uses two completely different roots. A single utterance is one finished speech event: perfective сказала. The fem -ла agrees with Маша.

items.promptEnglish: Anton has already finished the article.
items.hint: 'Уже' (already) is a completion cue. Subject Антон is masculine.
items.explanation: 'Уже' marks completion: the article is finished. Perfective прочитал, masc -л to agree with Антон.

items.promptEnglish: Lena was writing a letter all day.
items.hint: 'Весь день' (all day) is a duration cue. Subject Лена is feminine.
items.explanation: Duration → imperfective. Bare verb писала, fem -ла to agree with Лена. The perfective написала would say the letter got finished, which 'all day' does not claim.

items.promptEnglish: We learned the lesson by morning.
items.hint: 'К утру' (by morning) is a deadline cue. Subject 'мы' is plural.
items.explanation: Deadline cues mark completion: by morning the lesson was known. Perfective выучили, plural -ли. Pair: учить (imperfective) / выучить (perfective); the perfective adds the prefix вы-.

items.promptEnglish: Masha was cooking dinner all morning.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1's logic: 'all morning' duration cue and a feminine subject.
items.explanation: Duration → imperfective; Маша (fem) → -ла. Готовила marks the cooking process; приготовила would mark a finished result, which the sentence does not claim.

items.promptEnglish: Anton finished the work and went home.
items.hint: Sequence: did the work, then went home. Masculine subject.
items.explanation: A sequence of finished events implies the first action is complete before the next begins. Perfective сделал, masc -л to agree with Антон. The pair is делать / сделать (prefix с-).

items.promptEnglish: Masha did her homework for two hours.
items.hint: The duration cue 'два часа' stays. Which aspect fits a process?
items.explanation: The bare duration 'два часа' frames the homework as a process, which takes the imperfective past: делала (feminine -ла). Сделала would claim a completed result, clashing with the duration phrase.

items.prompt: Антон _____ кофе и пошёл на работу.
items.promptEnglish: Anton drank up his coffee and went to work.
items.hint: The 'и пошёл' sequence needs a finished first step.
items.explanation: The sequence 'did X and then went' requires the first action to be completed, so the perfective past выпил. Пил would leave the drinking open-ended, which cannot precede 'и пошёл' as a finished step.

items.promptEnglish: I (f) have already got dinner ready.
items.hint: Pair: готовить / приготовить. The dinner got DONE. Fem speaker.
items.explanation: The result reading ('got it ready') takes the perfective past: приготовила (feminine -ла). Готовила would describe the cooking process without the finished result; приготовлю is the future.

blanks: Маша и Антон _____ книгу за день. (Masha and Anton read the book through in a day.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'За день' (in a day) is a perfective time-frame cue. Subject 'Маша и Антон' is plural, so the ending is -ли. Прочитали is the perfective past plural.

errorCorrection.sentence: Соня спела песню, когда отключили микрофон.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Sonya was singing a song when they switched off the microphone.
errorCorrection.explanation: An action already in progress when something interrupts it takes the imperfective: пела shows the singing was underway, and 'отключили микрофон' is the completed event that cut in. Perfective спела means 'sang the song all the way through', which cannot be the ongoing background to an interruption. The interrupted action is imperfective; the interrupting one is perfective.

errorCorrection.sentence: Вечером он пришёл домой, ужинал и лёг спать.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In the evening he came home, had dinner, and went to bed.
errorCorrection.explanation: A chain of consecutive completed actions ('came home, had dinner, went to bed') takes the perfective for each step: поужинал presents dinner as one finished event, matching пришёл and лёг. Imperfective ужинал would describe dinner as an ongoing process ('was having dinner'), which breaks the 'and then' chain of results. When actions happen one after another to completion, Russian uses the perfective throughout.

errorCorrection.sentence: Раньше в школе мы часто написали диктанты.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Back in school we often wrote dictations.
errorCorrection.explanation: Часто marks a repeated habit, and repeated past actions take the imperfective: писали. Perfective написали presents the writing as one completed event, which cannot be 'often' repeated. Написали would fit a single occasion ('Мы написали диктант вчера'), not a habit.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha read the book through in an hour.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'За час' is a perfective time-frame cue. Subject Маша → -ла. Perfective прочитала; the imperfective читала would describe only the process and would not match 'in an hour.'
'Каждый вечер' (every evening) signals a HABIT or repeated action: imperfective. Смотрел, masc -л for Антон. The perfective посмотрел would describe a single completed viewing, not a habit.

reviewVocab.definition: past tense (the tense in which both Russian aspects coexist; the choice between them sharpens the meaning)
reviewVocab.example: Прошедшее время — главный контекст для выбора вида в русском языке.

reviewVocab.definition: agreement (the past-tense ending agrees with the subject's gender / number: -л, -ла, -ло, -ли)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша читала' согласование показывает женский род.

reviewVocab.definition: repetition, repeated action (a meaning of the imperfective; cues include каждый, иногда, часто)
reviewVocab.example: Антон каждый вечер смотрел телевизор: повторение, поэтому несовершенный вид.
